name: Zapier
shortDescription: Connects thousands of apps so work happens automatically, with AI steps.
bestFor: Connecting apps and automating work without code, the easy way
about: Zapier connects your apps so that something in one app triggers an action in another. For example, a new Google Form answer can be added to a Google Sheet and sent to you on Slack, with no code.
It works with thousands of apps and can add AI steps, such as summarising an email or sorting a message.
useCases: Save form answers to a spreadsheet
Get notified of new orders or leads
Summarise emails with AI and send them to Slack
features: Build automations by describing them in plain words

howToUse.title: Sign up
howToUse.text: Create a free account at zapier.com.

howToUse.title: Describe your automation
howToUse.text: Type what you want, such as "when I get a new Gmail with an invoice, save the attachment to Google Drive".

howToUse.title: Connect your apps
howToUse.text: Sign in to each app so Zapier can use it.

howToUse.title: Test it
howToUse.text: Run a test with real data and check the result.

howToUse.title: Turn it on
howToUse.text: Publish the Zap. It now runs by itself.

tips: Start with one simple automation that saves you time every day.
Each action counts as a task, so long workflows use your monthly limit faster.
limitations: The free plan has a small monthly task limit.
It gets expensive with lots of tasks.
pricingNote: US prices. The price goes up with more tasks.

name: Make
shortDescription: Visual automation builder for connecting apps and AI, cheaper than Zapier.
bestFor: Bigger, more complex automations at a lower price than Zapier
about: Make (formerly Integromat) lets you build automations on a visual canvas: you drag app modules and connect them in a flow, with branches, filters and loops.
It is cheaper than Zapier for large amounts of work, but takes a little longer to learn.
useCases: Process orders from an online shop
AI workflows, such as writing replies to messages
Move data between apps on a schedule

howToUse.title: Sign up
howToUse.text: Create a free account at make.com.

howToUse.title: Start from a template
howToUse.text: Search for a template close to what you need.

howToUse.title: Connect modules
howToUse.text: Add apps as modules and connect them in order.

howToUse.title: Run once to test
howToUse.text: Click Run once and check what each module did.

howToUse.title: Schedule it
howToUse.text: Turn on the scenario and set how often it runs.

tips: Use filters so the scenario only continues when it should.
Check the credit use of each run before scheduling it often.
limitations: Credits expire at the end of each period.
freePlanDetails: A small number of free credits each month.
pricingNote: US prices. Sources showed $9 to $12 per month billed yearly, so check the website.

name: n8n
shortDescription: Workflow automation and AI agents you can host yourself for free.
bestFor: Technical users who want powerful automations and AI agents, free if self-hosted
about: n8n is a workflow automation tool, similar to Zapier and Make, that is very popular for building AI agents. You can use the paid cloud version, or host it yourself for free.
It allows code inside workflows, so developers can do almost anything with it.
useCases: AI agents that answer messages or emails
features: Code nodes for JavaScript and Python

howToUse.title: Choose cloud or self-host
howToUse.text: Start a cloud trial at n8n.io, or install it on your own server or computer for free.

howToUse.title: Create a workflow
howToUse.text: Add a trigger, such as a webhook, a schedule or a new message.

howToUse.title: Add nodes
howToUse.text: Add app and AI nodes and connect them.

howToUse.title: Test each step
howToUse.text: Run the workflow and check the output of each node.

howToUse.title: Activate
howToUse.text: Turn the workflow on so it runs by itself.

tips: Import a community template to learn faster.
Keep API keys in n8n credentials, never inside the workflow text.
limitations: Self-hosting needs technical knowledge and a server.
The cloud plan counts every workflow run, so frequent triggers add up.
freePlanDetails: Free if you host it yourself. The cloud version has a free trial.
